strategy.title: Ensuring American Space Superiority (Executive Order 14369)
strategy.owner: Executive Office of the President; APST coordinates implementation (EO 14369 Sec. 3(a))
strategy.summary: Executive Order 14369, signed 18 December 2025, sets national space priorities for civil exploration, security, commercial growth and space research. It directs a crewed return to the Moon by 2028, initial elements of a lunar outpost by 2030, and a space security strategy within 180 days. It revokes EO 14056, which created the National Space Council, and assigns coordination to the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology.
strategy.budget: The EO sets no appropriation. Congress approved continuing appropriations for FY2027 on 2 September 2026 (P.L. 119-103), and the sources opened say NASA is held at its FY2026 level of USD 24.4 billion through 11 December 2026 (SpacePolicyOnline, secondary). The FY2027 request figures for NASA and the Space Force were not verified against primary budget documents in this run.
goals: Return Americans to the Moon by 2028 through the Artemis Program (EO Sec. 2(a)(i))
Establish initial elements of a permanent lunar outpost by 2030 (EO Sec. 2(a)(ii))
Prototype next-generation missile defence technologies by 2028 (EO Sec. 2(b)(i))
Attract at least USD 50 billion of additional investment in American space markets by 2028 (EO Sec. 2(c)(i))
Create a commercial pathway to replace the International Space Station by 2030 (EO Sec. 2(c)(iii))
Deploy a lunar surface nuclear reactor ready for launch by 2030 (EO Sec. 2(d)(ii))
strategy.law: Executive order, not a statute. EO 14369 is in the Federal Register (Vol. 90, No. 244, 23 December 2025). Statutes cited in the seed (National Aeronautics and Space Act 1958; Commercial Space Launch Act 1984) were not opened in this run.

strategy.title: Programa Espacial Mexicano 2026-2030
strategy.owner: Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones (ATDT), with the Agencia Espacial Mexicana as technical authority
strategy.summary: Published in the DOF on 4 June 2026 under the ATDT as issuing body. It is aligned with the Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2025-2030 and the ATDT sectoral programme. Initial projects: a new national telecommunications satellite to connect remote localities; a constellation of small Earth observation satellites for civil protection, environment, agriculture and territorial planning; a national centre to process satellite imagery; training of specialists; and international cooperation, including ITU coordination of orbital positions and spectrum rights. It follows a period in which the AEM was restructured under the ATDT and left without a titular head (per March 2026 reporting).
strategy.budget: No dedicated budget figure for the 2026-2030 programme is stated in the programme text. Expansión (8 Jan 2026) reports the 2026 federal budget allocation to the AEM as 46,755 millones de pesos, a 33.1% cut from 69,950 million in 2025. The unit reading is unresolved: the seed's 'MXN 46.8 million' differs from the printed figure.
goals: Build a new national telecommunications satellite to connect remote localities
Deploy a constellation of small Earth observation satellites for civil protection, environment, agriculture, security and territorial planning
Create a national centre to process and analyse satellite imagery from national and commercial systems
Train Mexican specialists for the space sector
Link Mexico to the international space sector and strengthen management of orbital positions and spectrum rights at the ITU
strategy.law: No comprehensive national space activities law was found in the sources opened. The Ley que crea la Agencia Espacial Mexicana (DOF 30 Jul 2010) creates the AEM as a decentralised public body; its 2010 sector reference (Secretaría de Comunicaciones y Transportes) is superseded by the ATDT reform as stated in the 2026 programme. Constitutional basis: CPEUM arts. 26 and 28, as cited in the programme.

strategy.title: Exploration, Imagination, Innovation: A New Space Strategy for Canada
strategy.status: under revision (a replacement is being prepared; a Special Adviser on Space was appointed 21 Oct 2026)
strategy.horizon: No fixed end date in the 2019 document; dated commitments include the ESA agreement to 2030 and LEAP funding over five years
strategy.owner: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (Minister of Industry), delivered largely through the Canadian Space Agency
strategy.summary: The 2019 strategy names space a strategic national asset and sets five priorities, the first being Canada's contribution to the US-led Lunar Gateway. It commits CAD 1.9 billion to an AI-enabled deep-space robotic system, CAD 150 million over five years to the Lunar Exploration Accelerator Program, and renews the ESA cooperation agreement to 2030. CP24 reported on 21 Oct 2026 that the Minister of Industry described a new space strategy in preparation at SpaceBound 2026, and the Prime Minister named astronaut Jeremy Hansen as Special Adviser on Space on 21 Oct 2026. No replacement strategy text has been published in the sources opened.
strategy.budget: The 2019 strategy commits CAD 1.9 billion to the Gateway robotic system and CAD 150 million over five years to LEAP; a 2018 announcement (cited in the strategy) provided CAD 100 million over five years for LEO broadband. National Defence committed CAD 200 million for a 10-year launch pad lease and CAD 105 million in Launch the North grants in March 2026. No replacement strategy budget is published.
goals: Ensure Canada remains a leading spacefaring nation by joining the Lunar Gateway mission
Inspire the next generation of Canadians to reach for the stars
Harness space to solve everyday challenges for Canadians
Position Canada's commercial space sector to grow the economy and create jobs
Ensure Canada's leadership in acquiring and using space-based data
strategy.law: No comprehensive national space act. The Canadian Space Agency Act (S.C. 1990, c. 13; consolidated version current to 30 Sep 2026) applies. Commercial launch is handled case by case under the interim approach announced in January 2023. Bill C-28 (Canadian Space Launch Act) would amend the Aeronautics Act; its status is unverified in the primary record. ISED published a consultation on a new Space Act on 20 Oct 2026 (announced 22 Oct); comments are due 21 Dec 2026 per a law-firm summary.

strategy.summary: The 4th Basic Plan was decided in December 2022 (seed) and covers 2023-2027 with a goal of a major space economy by 2045 (seed). Implementation runs through KASA annual work plans. The 2026 KASA work plan sets priorities including Nuri launches under a block-buy contract, a feasibility study on a LEO satellite communications network, a lunar communication orbiter via Nuri by 2029, and reusable launch vehicles by the 2030s. Launch a lunar communication orbiter via Nuri by 2029 (KASA 2026 work plan)
Complete preliminary design of a next-generation launch vehicle in 2026 and secure reusable launch vehicles by the 2030s (KASA 2026 work plan)
Establish the Republic of Korea Aerospace Industry Promotion Strategy (tentative) and develop field-oriented talent (KASA 2026 work plan)
Expand the National Space Council into a National Aerospace Council (proposed in KASA 2026 work plan)

Current timeline per Taipei Times (16 Oct 2026): TASA says the second FORMOSAT-8 satellite (FS-8B) has been assembled and completed environmental testing and is expected to launch in the first quarter of next year (2027); FS-8A image quality exceeded original goals. strategy.budget: Seed figure, not re-proved: Phase III expected cost NT$25.1 billion (about US$814 million) for 2019 to 2028; TASA annual budget about NT$3.7 billion in 2023 and NT$4.4 billion in 2024. No current (2026) budget figure proved in this run.
goals: Deploy the eight-satellite FORMOSAT-8 optical constellation by 2031; FS-8B expected to launch in the first quarter of 2027 (Taipei Times, 16 Oct 2026)
Develop synthetic aperture radar and ultra high resolution optical satellites (seed, not re-proved)
Build a domestic LEO communications capability through the B5G LEO satellite programme (seed, not re-proved)
Raise domestic content of satellites and expand into rockets and launch services (seed, not re-proved)
Establish a national launch site in Pingtung County (seed, not re-proved)
Grow international cooperation, notably with the United States, Japan and European partners (seed, not re-proved)

strategy.status: unverified (seed: in force; legal database shows effect status 'known')
strategy.owner: Prime Minister (issuing body); Ministry of Science and Technology leads civil-sector implementation
strategy.summary: Decision 169/QD-TTg, issued 4 Feb 2021 by the Prime Minister, promulgates the strategy to 2030 and succeeds the 2006 national strategy. It targets a mid-level position in Southeast Asia by 2030 (VGP, 13 Mar 2026), replacement of the VINASAT-1 and VINASAT-2 telecom satellites, mastery of small high-resolution Earth observation satellites and a larger space workforce. At the 13 Mar 2026 inauguration of the Vietnam National Space Center the government restated the targets and said it is moving toward a national space law.
strategy.budget: No consolidated national space budget proved in this run (seed claim, absence not re-proved). Vietnam National Space Center: total investment over VND 7 trillion (over US$266.2 million), the first high-tech science project financed by a Japanese government ODA loan (VGP, 13 Mar 2026).
goals: Reach a mid-level position in space science and technology in Southeast Asia by 2030 (VGP, 13 Mar 2026, partial quote)
Replace the VINASAT-1 and VINASAT-2 telecommunications satellites (Decision 169 text)
Train about 300 space experts and about 3,000 space engineers by 2030 (Decision 169 text)
Upgrade about 10 specialised laboratories and develop about 5 space science groups and 15 space technology groups (Decision 169 text)
Master technology for small, high-resolution Earth observation satellites (seed, consistent with Decision 169 text)
Develop domestic and overseas markets for satellite imagery and transmission services (seed, not re-proved)
strategy.law: No national space law in force (VGP, 13 Mar 2026: the government will continue to improve institutions and policies governing space activities, moving toward the development of a national space law). strategy.title: National Space Plan 2026-2032 (Národní kosmický plán 2026-2032)
strategy.owner: Government of the Czech Republic; drafted under the Ministry of Transport and administered by the Ministry of Industry and Trade since 1 March 2026
strategy.summary: Approved by the government on 22 October 2025 as the fourth national space plan. Vision: the Czech Republic as an active, internationally recognised space actor. Four priority areas: (1) strategic lines and competence platforms, (2) promising technologies, (3) the supporting space ecosystem, (4) institutionalisation of space activities, including a target of a Czech Space Agency by the end of 2032.
strategy.budget: Indicative financing table (Annex 6, mil. CZK): total 3,170 in 2026 and 2027, then 2,370 a year for 2028-2032. Mandatory ESA activities 400 a year (paid from MŠMT); optional ESA programmes minimum 1,470 a year; the ESA framework project 1,300 in 2026 and 2027 including the ISS mission (800 a year in those years). Government Resolution No. 365 of 21 May 2025 provides for a CZK 1,600 million ESA contribution for the mission in 2026-2027. Amounts are indicative and depend on the CZK/EUR rate.
goals: Define strategic lines of development and create competence platforms (priority area 1)
Support perspective space technologies (priority area 2)
Strengthen the supporting space ecosystem and use of space data (priority area 3)
Institutionalise space activities: transform VZLÚ and establish a Czech Space Agency by end-2032 (priority area 4)
strategy.law: No national space act found in this run. The plan text contains no reference to a space act. The e-Sbírka legal database was NOT checked in this run, so the absence is provisional (flagged).

strategy.owner: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications (MKM); delivered by the Estonian Space Office in EIS
strategy.summary: Programme vision: a strong partner in European space programmes, with Estonia leading in space services for decision-making, autonomous robotics and space cybersecurity. strategy.budget: Programme cost table (Table 6) totals EUR 90,780,000 for 2020–2027; the text says the realistic full cost will be under EUR 80 million because the funding target will not be reached from 2020. ESA contribution: EUR 2.7 million in 2019, target EUR 10 million a year by 2027. No appropriation in the state budget verified in this run.
goals: Public sector and public services: space services centre and use of space data
Technology entrepreneurship and space industrial policy
Education and science in space
International cooperation, with ESA and the EU space programme
Programme management through the Space Affairs Council and the Estonian Space Office
strategy.law: No national space act in force. A draft Estonian Space Act (Eesti kosmoseseadus) went to public consultation in Sept 2024 with a planned entry into force of 1 Jan 2026 (MKM news, 26.09.2024); MKM submitted the draft to government in August 2026 (Tööstusuudised, 18.08.2026; ERR News, 13.08.2026). Double above-threshold Horizon Europe space proposals and place Latvian researchers in ESA science mission teams (seed; not fully re-read)

strategy.owner: Ministry responsible for the economy: Ministry of the Economy, Tourism and Sport at adoption (3 Nov 2023); now the Ministry of Economy, Labour and Sport
strategy.summary: The government adopted Slovenia's first space strategy on 3 November 2023 after an 18-month process run by the newly established Slovenian Space Office. It covers 2023–2030, sets five strategic pillars (technology and R&D, international exploration, applications, STEM talent, and entrepreneurship and spin-offs), and links the sector to ESA, EU programmes and the 2022 space act. The PDF in hand is headed 'REVISED DRAFT'; the adopted-text identity is flagged.
strategy.budget: Approximately EUR 20 million in ESA contributions for 2023–2025 (strategy text). The later ESA membership fee figures in the seed were not re-read. No overall national space budget was found in the sources opened.
goals: Encourage and evolve space technologies and R&D, including satellite communication on Earth and beyond
Broaden participation in responsible international space exploration and research
Foster the development and uptake of space applications for a stronger commercial and sustainable future
Secure the future generation of scientists, engineers and young space professionals (STEM)
Stimulate entrepreneurship and university and RTO spin-offs through dedicated space innovation programmes
strategy.law: Space Activities Act (Zakon o vesoljskih dejavnostih, ZVDej), Uradni list RS 43/2022 of 25 March 2022, adopted by the National Assembly on 16 March 2022. Permits are issued by 'the ministry responsible for technology' (art. 4); the Act sets the register of launched space objects.
